description: Na₂FeO₄ is Sylvanite-like structured and crystallizes in the orthorhombic Pnnm space group. There are two inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.31-2.53 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted NaO₆ octahedra that share corners with four equivalent NaO₆ octahedra, corners with four equivalent FeO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one FeO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 27°. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.35-2.76 Å. Fe is bonded to four O atoms to form FeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four equivalent NaO₆ octahedra and  an edgeedge with one NaO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 8-72°. There are two shorter (1.66 Å) and two longer (1.67 Å) Fe-O bond lengths. There are three inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to three Na and one Fe atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to three Na and one Fe atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to three Na and one Fe atom.
